thread:
Anya: Quick question — we're hitting a lot of edge cases around the browser SDKs and internal services during the proto->gRPC push. Thinking about adding 'escape hatches' in routing so clients can force JSON fallback per-request (for browser) or pin to grpc for server-to-server. Also need canary UX for routing policy (percentages per-tenant), and telemetry hooks to detect fallback reasons and quota burn. Thoughts?

Sam: +1 for the escape hatch header. Maybe "X-Redwood-Transport: grpc|json". Gateway can rewrite/forward. Keep the kernel simple — prefer a header over URL params. :thumbsup:

Mohit: Can we implement as a two-layer policy: default routing (policy engine) + per-request overrides only allowed when the tenant has a "dev-transport-override" flag? That prevents accidental wide blast. Also need Console controls to set tenant-level overrides and to view the "route decision" timeline. :eyes:

Anya: Good call. Telemetry fields I'd want emitted for every request:
- route_elected: grpc/json
- fallback_reason: header_missing | proto_unavailable | timeout | validation_error
- decision_path: policy | override | fallback
We should emit these as structured logs/traces and expose them in Console's request inspector and in the rollout dashboard.

Sam: Envoy header rewrite + simple match rule will handle most of the routing. Example (pseudo):
```
# envoy filter (pseudo)
match: { header: "X-Redwood-Transport", value_present: true }
action: route_to: "json-gateway"
```
Also watch out: json fallback disables KV prefix caching on the server (can't use binary kv cache), so it increases token cost per-request — we should flag a per-tenant cost delta in the Console early in the canary. :zap:

Mohit: For proto vs json contract: prefer auto-transcode with annotations so we don't duplicate schemas. Gateway should transcode and validate using the same proto descriptors. If a numeric field is unknown or type-mismatch, return 400 with a clear code (PROTO_VALIDATION) instead of silently falling back.

Anya: Migration plan sketch:
1) Add header support + opt-in tenant flag (dev tenants only)
2) Start 1% canary across prod with telemetry capture for fallback_reason + latency + cost
3) Surface a rollout card in Console that shows routed_by histogram, top fallback reasons, latency delta, and a single-click "rollback" that flips the tenant flag
4) Auto-rollback if error rate > 0.5% or cost delta > 15% over 1h
5) After 2 weeks and stable metrics, allow targeted percentages per tenant group (10/25/50)
I'd like a tiny dashboard mock for step 3 — simple heatmap + top reasons list.

Sam: Example client curl to force json: 
```
curl -H "X-Redwood-Transport: json" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer ..."
```

deploy-bot: deployd web-gateway v2 -> staging succeeded :white_check_mark:

Mohit: Also add a tracing span name "transport.choose" with attribute "route" and "fallback_reason" so we can build cross-service heatmaps in Tempo/Jaeger.

Anya: OK I'll draft the RFC + the tiny Console mock this afternoon and link it here. Thanks everyone :+1:

Sam: happy to help with the envoy filter and telemetry pipeline. :shipit:
